facts: It is the morning of the Hollyfield village dog show on the village green.
Mrs. Finch, the judge, put the big blue Best in Show rosette on the judges' table in the marquee at half past nine.
At ten to eleven Mrs. Finch came back to the judges' table and the blue rosette was gone.
The prizes are meant to be given out at eleven o'clock.
It is a dry, sunny morning, and the grass on the green is dry.
Mrs. Dove from the tea stall carried the judges their tea this morning.
Oliver's spaniel Pepper won the blue rosette last year, and Oliver was heard saying he wished Pepper could have it again.
People at the show are whispering about Oliver.

timeline: 9:00: Mr. Okafor opens the dog-washing tent and starts washing the dogs for the show, one after another. The wash tubs overflow onto the grass by the tent door and make a mud puddle, the only mud on the dry green.

9:30: Mrs. Finch puts the big blue Best in Show rosette on the white tablecloth of the judges' table in the marquee, beside a plate of six currant buns for the judges, and goes off to look at the dogs.
10:10: Oliver slips into the empty marquee, takes one of the judges' currant buns from the plate and eats it behind the prize table. The blue rosette is still on the judges' table.
10:15: Oliver comes out of the marquee licking his fingers. Mrs. Dove sees him from the tea stall. She gives him the job of stacking paper cups, and he stays at the tea stall until ten to eleven.

10:20: Tilly's old dog Biscuit, waiting for his bath at the dog-washing tent, rolls in the mud puddle by the tent door and gets muddy from nose to tail. Every other dog in the show has already been washed clean.

10:25: Mrs. Dove carries the judges' pot of tea to the marquee and sees the blue rosette still on the judges' table. Oliver minds the tea stall while she is gone. She is back at the tea stall by 10:28.
10:25 to 10:40: Mr. Okafor scrubs a big sheepdog in the far tub with his back to the tent door.

10:30: Tilly takes muddy Biscuit into the empty marquee. Biscuit puts a muddy front paw up on the judges' table and leaves a muddy paw print on the white tablecloth beside the rosette. Tilly takes the blue rosette and hurries back to the dog-washing tent.
10:35: Behind the towel rack in the dog-washing tent, Tilly pins the blue rosette on Biscuit's collar and tells him he is a winner.

10:42: Mr. Okafor calls Biscuit for his bath. He sees Tilly unpin something blue and frilly from Biscuit's collar and push it into Biscuit's red dog bag under a towel, so it will stay dry. A little mud from Biscuit's collar smudges the rosette's ribbons.
10:50: Mrs. Finch finds the judges' table empty and cries out that the rosette is gone. Tilly hears and is too frightened to take it back.
The blue rosette is safe and dry, wrapped in a towel in Biscuit's red dog bag in the dog-washing tent.
truth.motive: Biscuit is fourteen, this is his very last dog show, and in all his shows he has never won a single rosette. Tilly knew he would not win today either, so she took the Best in Show rosette to let him wear it just once and feel like a winner. She meant no harm, and then she was too frightened to give it back.

marquee.name: The Marquee
facts: The marquee is a big white tent in the middle of the village green.
The judges' table stands at the far end, covered with a white tablecloth.
A plate of currant buns for the judges sits on the judges' table.
A prize table with red, yellow and green rosettes stands beside it.

washing_tent.name: The Dog-Washing Tent
facts: The dog-washing tent is a striped tent with three big wash tubs inside.
It smells of soap and wet dog.
A towel rack full of fluffy towels stands at the back.
Water from the tubs has spilled out onto the grass by the tent door.

spots.name: the mud puddle by the tent door

tea_stall.name: The Tea Stall
facts: The tea stall is a table under a little awning, with a steaming tea urn.
Towers of paper cups and a big cake tin sit on the counter.
From the tea stall you can see the door of the marquee.

oliver.name: Oliver
oliver.personality: Bouncy, proud of his spaniel Pepper and very fond of cake. When he is worried about being told off he talks fast and changes the subject.

demeanor.guarded: Cheerful on the outside but jumpy, brushing at his jumper and talking about Pepper instead of the morning.
demeanor.shaken: Red in the face and sorry, mumbling about the bun.
demeanor.cleared: Relieved and keen to help find the rosette for whoever wins it.

knows.fact: Oliver's dog is a brown and white spaniel called Pepper.
Mrs. Dove runs the tea stall and makes the best cakes in the village.

appearance: Oliver is a boy of nine with sticking-up hair.
He wears a striped jumper and holds Pepper's lead.

dove.name: Mrs. Dove
dove.personality: Warm, chatty and busy, always pouring tea. She notices who comes and goes from the marquee door, but she is fair and does not like gossip.

demeanor.open: Friendly and talkative, wiping her hands on her apron as she answers.

knows.fact: Mrs. Dove has run the tea stall at the dog show for twenty years.
Mr. Okafor washes the dogs in the dog-washing tent before the show.

appearance: Mrs. Dove is a round, rosy-cheeked lady with silver hair in a bun.
She wears a flowery apron with a tea towel over her shoulder.

okafor.name: Mr. Okafor
okafor.personality: Calm, kind and patient with every dog. He answers carefully and only says what he saw himself.

demeanor.open: Easygoing and soapy, happy to chat while he rinses a tub.

knows.fact: Mr. Okafor washes the dogs for the show every year.
Dogs must be clean and dry before they go into the marquee to be judged.

appearance: Mr. Okafor is a tall man with a short grey beard.
He wears a long rubber apron and green wellies, both splashed with soapy water.

tilly.name: Tilly
tilly.personality: Gentle and shy, and she loves her old dog Biscuit more than anything. She is a poor liar: when she is scared she goes quiet and stares at her wellies.

demeanor.guarded: Quiet and polite, but she keeps standing in front of Biscuit's bag.
demeanor.shaken: Her lip wobbles and she hugs Biscuit tight.
demeanor.cornered: Tearful, with nothing left to hide behind.
demeanor.cleared: Sorry and relieved, wanting to give the rosette back straight away.

knows.fact: Biscuit is a scruffy little terrier with one ear that flops down.

appearance: Tilly is a small girl of seven with freckles and two plaits.
She wears a green raincoat and red wellies, and holds a damp, scruffy little terrier called Biscuit.

clue_paw_print.fact: On the white tablecloth of the judges' table, right beside the empty place where the blue rosette lay, there is one small muddy dog's paw print. The mud is brown and still a little damp. Somebody's dog put its muddy paw up on the table.

clue_bun_crumbs.fact: The judges' bun plate has room for six currant buns but only five are left. A trail of currant crumbs leads from the plate to behind the prize table.

clue_puddle.fact: Water from the wash tubs has made a big mud puddle on the grass by the door of the dog-washing tent. It is the only mud on the whole dry green. In the middle is a squashed patch where a small dog has rolled.

source.spot: the mud puddle by the tent door

clue_rosette_in_bag.fact: Inside Biscuit's red dog bag, wrapped in a towel, is the big blue Best in Show rosette, safe and dry. Its blue ribbons have little smudges of brown mud on them.

clue_order_book.fact: Mrs. Dove's order book at the tea stall says: 'Judges' pot of tea, to the marquee, 10:25.'

oliver_never_inside.fact: Oliver says he had not been inside the marquee at all this morning until just now, and that he would never take the rosette.
oliver_never_inside.why: Oliver did go into the marquee at ten past ten to eat one of the judges' currant buns, and he does not want to be told off for it.

tell_oliver_crumbs.fact: Oliver has currant crumbs down the front of his striped jumper, and he keeps brushing them off when he thinks nobody is looking.

oliver_admits_bun.fact: Oliver admits he slipped into the empty marquee at ten past ten and ate one of the judges' currant buns behind the prize table. The blue rosette was still on the judges' table when he came out at quarter past ten, and after that he went to the tea stall to help Mrs. Dove.

line.text: Ask Oliver kindly whether he ate something he should not have, and say a bun is not the end of the world.

dove_saw_oliver.fact: Mrs. Dove says that at quarter past ten she saw Oliver come out of the marquee licking his fingers and looking very pleased with himself.

dove_rosette_at_tea.fact: Mrs. Dove says she carried the judges' pot of tea into the marquee at twenty-five past ten, and the blue rosette was still on the judges' table then. Nobody else was in the marquee.

reached.about: the judges' tea and the rosette

dove_oliver_helped.fact: Mrs. Dove says that from quarter past ten until ten to eleven Oliver stayed at the tea stall stacking paper cups. He minded the stall while she took the judges' tea at twenty-five past ten, and he was still there when she came back. He never went back to the marquee.

reached.about: where Oliver was after quarter past ten

okafor_washed_dogs.fact: Mr. Okafor says he has washed every dog in the show this morning, one after another since nine o'clock. Old Biscuit was the last dog, and he washed him at quarter to eleven.

okafor_biscuit_mud.fact: Mr. Okafor says that at twenty past ten, while he waited for his bath, Biscuit rolled in the mud puddle by the tent door and got muddy from nose to tail. Every other dog had already been washed clean, so from twenty past ten until his bath at quarter to eleven Biscuit was the only dog on the green with muddy paws.

reached.about: muddy dogs and the mud puddle

okafor_saw_blue.fact: Mr. Okafor says that at about twenty to eleven, when he called Biscuit for his bath, he saw Tilly unpin something blue and frilly from Biscuit's collar and push it into Biscuit's red dog bag under a towel.

reached.about: Tilly and Biscuit's red dog bag

tilly_alibi.fact: Tilly says she and Biscuit stayed in the dog-washing tent all morning and never went near the marquee.
tilly_alibi.why: Tilly took Biscuit into the marquee at half past ten and took the rosette, and she is frightened of getting into trouble.

tell_tilly_bag.fact: Tilly keeps standing in front of Biscuit's red dog bag and glancing down at it, as if to check it is still shut.

tilly_last_show.fact: Tilly says Biscuit is fourteen, today is his very last dog show, and he has never won a single rosette in his whole life.

tilly_admits_marquee.fact: Tilly admits that she and Biscuit did go into the marquee at half past ten, when nobody was there, and muddy Biscuit put his front paw up on the judges' table.

tilly_confession.fact: Tilly says she took the blue rosette from the judges' table at half past ten. Biscuit has never won anything and this is his last show, so she wanted him to wear it just once. She pinned it on his collar behind the towel rack, then hid it in his red dog bag before his bath to keep it dry. When she heard Mrs. Finch cry out, she was too frightened to give it back.

oliver_cleared.text: Oliver is cleared: the rosette was still on the judges' table at twenty-five past ten, and from quarter past ten until it was found gone Oliver was at the tea stall with Mrs. Dove.

bun_explained.text: Oliver sneaked into the marquee for one of the judges' currant buns, not for the rosette. That is why he came out licking his fingers.
bun_explained.resolves: red herring: Oliver coming out of the marquee licking his fingers

culprit_tilly.text: Tilly took the blue rosette: muddy Biscuit's paw print was left on the judges' table, and the rosette was hidden in Biscuit's red dog bag.
